Loop-scope field reuse review (read-only)
Worktree /home/wishapig/hackathon-overnight/analysis, src/metadata.cpp versus baseline3429b75d70adb417588f0ecd6c583f32ba6abaa6. Final snapshot diff109 additions/6 deletions; owner changed the first one-pass design to post-lowering two-pass plan_scopes during review. Review conclusions refer to the latest two-pass source. Requirements v9 read fully. No compile, numerical run, profiling, or source edit by this reviewer.

Conclusion: no concrete blocking stale-value, pointer-lifetime, overflow/short-circuit or explicit work-limit bug found in the reviewed paths. This is static evidence, not functional/performance acceptance. Temporary trace and existing endpoint verification belong to owner/root.

1. Pointer stability (BoundExpr725, BoundNode741, nodes856-914, plan_scopes915-933):
Base lowering fully creates result.nodes before plan_scopes runs. Each nodes output vector is resized once to source.size before elements are populated. Call args and read/write region vectors finish resize and expression assignment before any FieldUpdate points into them. plan_loop_fields only resizes changing_fields and scope_calls vectors; neither contains the BoundNode/BoundExpr objects being pointed to. Thus plan creation cannot relocate target objects.
All FieldUpdate expression pointers refer to top-level call.args elements or BoundRegion members inside call.reads/writes storage. scope_calls stores pointers to Call elements inside stable body/otherwise vectors. Returning BoundProgram uses vector move construction, transferring owned buffers without element relocation; standard allocator vector movement in result.nodes and nested body assignment likewise transfers storage. Program is passed const and remains alive through execute_bound, so BoundExpr.source and BoundNode.source stay valid. Evaluator mutates values/scratch/flags only, never the bound tree vector capacities. No later mutation in the reviewed call path invalidates pointers.

2. Slot cutoff correctness and Let shadowing (796-802,848-875,1052-1069):
Slots are allocated monotonically by bind; parameters0/1 precede every loop. Each loop binds its induction variable before lowering its body, so its slot is <= every Let/For slot in that body. changes_with_loop marks every reference with slot>=loop.slot dynamic, as well as every unbound no_slot reference. This is conservative: even a constant Let inside the loop remains dynamic. An external variable slot below the cutoff is never assigned while one activation of the nearest loop runs: executable scalar stores are only Let-to-that-node's unique slot and For-to-that-node's unique induction slot.
Let expression lowering resolves old symbols before binding its fresh slot. Same textual name cannot create a write to an earlier slot; reverse symbol lookup resolves the newest lexical binding. The source compiler rejects shadowing/redefinition, but manually provided supported Metadata lowering still preserves its existing fresh-slot behavior. If arms receive separate Symbols copies, so branch-local Lets do not leak into later scope. Calls before a later same-name Let remain bound to their original slot. This optimization does not add source-language support or redefine those existing semantics.

3. Nested For and reset (915-921,1055-1071):
plan_scopes associates a Call with its nearest surrounding For, traversing If arms with the same loop and nested For bodies with the nested loop. At each nonempty For activation, all associated calls set fields_initialized=false before its first iteration. The flag deliberately remains true across iterations of that activation; induction/body-slot-dependent fields are always in the update plan.
For a call inside inner loop, outer variables may be cached during the inner activation, but every new entry from a later outer iteration resets that call. For zero-iteration loops, reset is skipped after first>=last; no call executes, so no cache is observed. The next nonempty activation resets before use. A call outside all loops has no plan and follows the original full-evaluation path.

4. If reached late and lazy error semantics (1074-1091):
Planning inspects expression structure but never evaluates it. An If-false call does not fill scratch or set initialized. When a branch first becomes executable, every original argument and region field is evaluated in original order, and every original region check runs before initialized becomes true. Therefore division-by-zero, unbound variables and overflow cannot be raised early solely by planning; neither are they hidden on the first executable visit. Calls in separate arms have separate scratch/flags.
If a call later becomes reachable again in the same activation, external cached inputs are unchanged by the slot proof; dynamic inputs are reevaluated. If it is not reached for the whole activation, nothing numerical is done. Callback publication still occurs for every actual call.

5. Intermediate overflow, short-circuit and region checks (955-1039):
The optimization caches entire fields, not algebraic subexpressions. A field depending on any current-loop/internal slot is reevaluated by the unchanged recursive eval, preserving operand order, short-circuit &&/||, int32/int64 intermediate overflow, division/modulo errors and checked loop increments. A field whose only inputs are unchanged external slots/literals is first evaluated normally at the actual Call. Only after that complete evaluation and all region checks succeed is its result reused. Since expression evaluation is pure and the inputs cannot change within that activation, it cannot newly overflow on a later iteration. No constant folding, reassociation or eager evaluation introduced.
FieldUpdate entries retain original ordering: dynamic args first, then each read's dynamic offset/rows/cols/stride followed by that read's check marker, then writes likewise. Invariant region coordinates retain their previously validated nonnegative values, while check_region reruns on the combined old invariant/new dynamic geometry in source order. Thus dynamic rows/cols/stride/offset cannot bypass the original combined bounds check. Entirely invariant call with args but no regions gets one null marker; update loop no-ops while publish still occurs. No invariants -> no plan -> original path.

6. max_steps and max_tasks (804,932,949-956,1041-1046):
When limits.max_steps is nonzero, lower does not call plan_scopes; plan_loop_fields additionally guards it. All changing_fields remain empty, so a full call leaves fields_initialized=false and every visit evaluates the original expression/region sequence. Added region helper does not call tick; original tick locations and error ordering are preserved. max_tasks and publish are unchanged, counting every call whether cached or not.
With max_steps=0, optimization intentionally reduces evaluator steps. The theoretical size_t overflow limit would count fewer steps, but no user maximum is imposed and no task/semantic work is skipped. No artificial iteration/task cap was added.

7. Resource accounting and scope (764-776,815-846):
New BoundNode vector/flag footprint is part of sizeof(BoundNode) charged by the existing lowerer. Plans and scope pointer capacities use take/resize, which double-charge retained storage; scope reserve leaves previous charge conservatively retained, covering reserve old/new peak. Planning occurs after base lowering, so optional plans cannot cause later base-lowering allocation failure. A plan that does not fit calculated remaining budget is skipped and the original evaluator is retained.
Nonblocking caveat: plans consume real memory and may reduce later task/temporary phase headroom; the guard guarantees the plan fits, not identical memory coverage to baseline. Global-new failure during optional planning still unwinds to the existing resource recovery; no special allocation suppression is present. Do not claim zero memory cost or identical low-budget thresholds. This review does not request a new fallback mechanism without actual evidence of a problem.

R28/Metadata: no serialized format/name/digest/audit addition. New state exists only in decoded binding structures and is needed for the proposed optimization. It does not hardcode Cholesky shapes, symbols, call patterns or case IDs.

Recommended existing temporary evidence, only within owner's authorized slot: output traces for nested reentry/zero loops/late If/Let scopes, invariant overflow reached versus unreachable and dynamic short-circuit expressions, explicit max_steps error-prefix parity, program/bound storage movement under sanitizers; full existing public20/R27 endpoint acceptance. These are coverage suggestions for the implementation change, not new permanent tests or added acceptance requirements.

Minimal distinct proposal approved by root: metadata.cpp-only nearest-For lazy field reuse. Binding-slot cutoff identifies dependencies on current loop/inside-let slots; n/b and outer slots invariant for one loop entry. Reset nearest-loop owned Calls on every For entry, then first actually reached Call executes original full evaluation; later executions use only varying top-level fields plus original per-region checks. No per-field generation/atomic checks. Nested calls reset only on their nearest loop entry. Calls outside loops unchanged. max_steps>0 uses exact old evaluator. If branches and empty loops are not eagerly evaluated. Original recursive evaluator preserves int32 intermediate overflow and short circuit; no algebraic rewrite or global CSE. Plan storage counts against BoundProgram. No Metadata/name/hash changes.
Old7de702a was same-call structural CSE; new proposal skips unchanged work across loop iterations with existing scratch outputs, not repeated structural matching. Old screening showed no reliable batch gain; this is a short distinct experiment only.
